title: Lender Preflight Coordination
name: Lender Preflight Coordination
metaTitle: Lender Preflight Coordination in Phoenix, AZ
metaDescription: Why financing needs to move before the 45-day deadline in a Phoenix 1031 exchange, and what a lender needs to preflight a replacement purchase.

sections.html:
Financing on a replacement property cannot wait until after the identification list is signed. Getting a lender to preflight the deal before day 45 is what keeps the 180-day exchange period from getting eaten up by underwriting delays later, and Phoenix underwriting timelines are not always as fast as investors expect.

A preflight is not a formal loan application, it is a straightforward conversation that puts a lender in a position to move quickly once a Phoenix candidate is finalized, rather than starting cold.

sections.heading: Why Financing Has to Move Before Day 45, Not After
sections.html:
Once a replacement property is identified, the clock keeps running regardless of how long it takes to get a loan approved. A multifamily deal in Chandler or Gilbert that looks straightforward on paper can still hit underwriting delays over rent roll verification or environmental review, and those delays do not pause the 180-day deadline for a Phoenix investor waiting on approval.

Even a well-qualified borrower can lose weeks to a lender's internal committee schedule, and those weeks come directly out of the time available to close, not out of some separate financing clock that runs independently of the exchange.

sections.heading: What a Lender Actually Needs to Preflight a Deal
sections.html:
Getting ahead of financing means having the lender's underwriting file mostly built before the identification notice even goes out, not scrambled together after a candidate property is picked. On a multifamily purchase, that means trailing financials on the target property and current information on the borrowing entity ready to hand over the moment a candidate firms up.

Lenders active across the Valley, from Camelback-area office deals to West Valley industrial purchases, are used to the exchange timeline, but that familiarity does not replace having the paperwork ready. A preflight conversation before day 45 gives the Phoenix lender a real shot at closing inside 180 days instead of asking for an extension no one can grant.

sections.heading: Matching Loan Terms to the Exchange Deadline
sections.html:
Rate locks, appraisal turnaround, and loan committee schedules all need to be checked against the exchange calendar, not merely against a general closing target. A 60-day rate lock does no good if the appraisal alone is going to take three weeks to schedule and complete in a busy Phoenix market.

Working backward from day 180, rather than forward from the day a candidate is identified, is the more reliable way to check whether a given lender's timeline actually fits a specific Phoenix purchase.

sections.heading: What a Preflight Package Actually Includes
sections.html:
Before approaching a lender on a candidate property, have the following ready:

  • Trailing 12-month financials and rent roll on the target property
  • Entity formation documents and a current personal financial statement
  • Existing debt schedule across the investor's portfolio
  • Realistic appraisal ordering timeline against the exchange deadline
  • Rate lock terms that extend past the expected closing date, not up to it

sections.heading: What Changes When Rates Are Moving
sections.html:
In a rate environment where terms can shift week to week, a Phoenix lender preflighting a multifamily or industrial purchase needs the borrower's file finalized fast, since a quote given on day 20 may not hold by day 45. Locking in terms too early can leave money on the table if rates improve, but waiting too long risks losing the rate that made the deal pencil out in the first place.

Coordinating this timing with the qualified intermediary and the lender together, rather than treating financing as a separate track from the exchange deadlines, is what keeps a Phoenix purchase from stalling in the final weeks.

faqs.q: Why can't I just start the loan process after I identify a property?
faqs.a: Waiting until after identification often means the loan process eats into time that should be spent closing, not underwriting. A preflight conversation before day 45 gives the lender a real head start.

faqs.q: What documents does a lender need to preflight a multifamily replacement purchase?
faqs.a: Trailing 12-month financials, a current rent roll, entity documents, a personal financial statement, and an existing debt schedule are typically the starting point for underwriting review.

faqs.q: How much time should I budget for a lender's appraisal?
faqs.a: Appraisal timelines vary by property type and lender, but should be confirmed and scheduled with enough buffer that a delay does not threaten the 180-day closing deadline for a Phoenix purchase.

faqs.q: Do rate locks matter for exchange timing?
faqs.a: Yes. A rate lock that expires before the realistic closing date can force a costly extension or a rate change late in the exchange, so lock terms should be matched against the exchange calendar, not merely the target closing date.

faqs.q: Should I preflight financing on more than one candidate property?
faqs.a: It is worth preflighting financing on every serious candidate on the identification list, since not every property will make it to closing and a lender relationship built early saves time if a backup candidate becomes the actual purchase.

faqs.q: Does preflighting financing cost anything before I pick a final property?
faqs.a: Some lenders will do a preliminary review at no cost, while others may charge a fee once formal underwriting begins. Confirm the specific terms with any Phoenix lender before assuming the preflight conversation is free.

faqs.q: What happens if my identified candidate does not appraise for the purchase price?
faqs.a: A low appraisal can force a renegotiation, a larger cash contribution, or a switch to a backup candidate on the list. Confirming realistic value expectations with the lender before day 45 reduces the odds of this surprise on a Phoenix purchase.
